title: Script-bound terminal workflow
intent: Turn a reviewed script and a later screen recording into a concise, readable agent-workflow edit with semantic camera moves, source-contiguous pacing, live terminal holds, and explicit proof beats.
applicability: The story is demonstrated through terminal, IDE, browser, or workflow UI states
A script can be reviewed before capture and every beat can later be bound to the immutable recording
contraindications: Presenter or talking-head footage is required
The workflow cannot be recorded without exposing secrets or private data
Source ranges and camera targets cannot be reviewed
required_evidence: screen.workflow.experience-receipt (when prior demo feedback changes the candidate)
rules: Keep script beats, captured source ranges, and final clips linked by stable ids
Start from the already-open clean terminal rather than showing desktop or workspace switching
Type every prompt once at real-time speed, then keep the completed prompt readable before the response
Move the camera only between semantic screen states and hold during reading or typing
Preserve prompt, action, and result anchors when compressing waits
Use source-contiguous speed tiers while one agent process remains in progress; do not hide source gaps behind transitions
Treat cursor blink, progress shimmer, monotonic timers, spinners, and mascot motion as live UI evidence
Use real source for a live hold or rebalance adjacent speeds; never freeze a full terminal frame that contains live UI
Keep reference media outside project assets and render lineage
Require human review of every post-capture source binding
Require a separate attributable review of machine-drafted voiceover timing
Admit session-derived lessons through a private immutable receipt and cite only its source-neutral projection hash publicly
heuristics: Establish wide before the first detail
Use 0.3s to 0.7s camera transitions and 2s to 5s read holds
Use smooth moves and gradual speed tiers within one screen context and hard cuts only between distinct states
Keep ordinary workflow compression at or below 24x; require an explicit reviewed risk override above it
Render visually complex finals in bounded source-contiguous segments when the full graph exceeds resource admission, then apply the continuous narration mix once
Place captions after camera transforms in the final-frame safe area
constraints: The pre-capture plan contains no source-media binding
The executable Treatment requires a reviewed edit spec
Legacy transform curves remain the video-safe baseline until Motion Language v2 video composition is proven
Reference-derived rules remain candidate defaults rather than Style Memory
Full-frame and region-aware temporal loops remain non-executable until their seam, timer, and QC contracts pass a generic evaluator
failure_modes: Wait compression removes the action or result anchor
A prompt appears as a flash, is repeated, or is rewound after typing
A 30x-plus segment reads as a cut even though its source is technically contiguous
A still hold freezes Working shimmer, cursor blink, elapsed time, or mascot animation
A full-frame loop repeats a monotonic timer or exposes a phase jump
Abrupt speed-tier changes make an otherwise continuous process feel cut
Terminal text is unreadable after scaling
Private data or notifications appear in capture
qc: Verify every plan beat has one or more ordered reviewed bindings
Review wide, transition, and result frames
Verify prompt entry appears once at real-time speed and the completed text remains readable
Verify every continuity group has no omitted or repeated source frame and preserves camera endpoints
Inspect live terminal regions during every hold; a static frame with a visible live signal is a failure
Warn on speeds above 24x and on speed-tier ratios that skip intermediate rates
When rendering in bounded segments, verify video continuity and mix or normalize narration only once
Check terminal text at delivery resolution
Check caption safe area after camera transforms
Check narration boundaries, speech continuity, and output loudness
Audit source lineage for reference hashes
positive_examples: A Codex terminal session structured as problem, prompt, action, diff, test, and result
An agent workflow where waiting is compressed but commands and proofs remain readable
A narration-led Codex session whose active work is continuously accelerated while Working shimmer and elapsed time remain alive
negative_examples: A presenter-led tutorial with occasional terminal overlays
An automatic cursor-follow crop with no reviewed semantic targets
A terminal walkthrough assembled from jump cuts inside one continuous agent response
A PNG hold that freezes the Working shimmer and elapsed timer

application_history.source_class: synthetic human-free screen recording plus synthetic narration
real human-free Codex terminal session with delivered narration

promotion_questions: Which transcript-to-beat mappings need more than segment-level review across technical narration styles?
What activity evidence best separates readable holds from non-informative waits?
When is a floating screen stage preferable to full-bleed capture?
Can a region-aware temporal hold preserve stable prompt text while phase-matching periodic shimmer and keeping timers monotonic?
Which visual-activity and semantic-density measurements should author smooth speed ramps rather than constant tiers?
What render-cost model should choose bounded video segments and one final narration mix before resource admission fails?
How many independently reviewed project demos are required before a candidate pacing rule can become a cross-project default?
